RULES.topic: NEW voter photo-ID requirement (Question 1, effective Jan. 1, 2026)
RULES.currentRule: Maine voters approved a first-time photo-ID requirement via the Question 1 citizen initiative (passed November 2025, effective January 1, 2026) — a major reversal of Maine's historical no-ID stance. Accepted ID for in-person voting: Maine driver's license, Maine non-driver ID, U.S. passport, military ID, or a concealed-carry permit with photo. College/university ID is explicitly NOT accepted. Absentee voters must include their ID number or a photocopy of their ID with their ballot return. Voters without ID cast a 'challenged ballot' and must provide ID within 4 days after the election, or sign a religious-exemption affidavit.
RULES.whyItMatters: This is the single most significant procedural change affecting ME-02 (and all Maine districts) for the 2026 cycle. Every ME-02 voter, including longtime Maine voters accustomed to no-ID voting, must now bring qualifying photo ID or be prepared to cast a challenged ballot and cure it within 4 days.
RULES.detail: NEEDS REVIEW: the specific implementing statute/administrative rule citation (Title 21-A section number) was not independently pulled from the Maine Legislature's enrolled-initiative text in this pass; corroborate against legislature.maine.gov before publishing exact ID-list wording. A dedicated Maine SOS voter-ID sub-page was also not isolated in this pass — substance is sourced to news/civic-tracker coverage of the initiative.

RULES.topic: Same-day voter registration (available through Election Day)
RULES.currentRule: Maine allows same-day voter registration in person at the municipal clerk's office, available up to and including Election Day itself. The standard mail/online registration deadline is 21 days before Election Day (Oct. 13, 2026 for the general election).
RULES.whyItMatters: ME-02 voters who miss the Oct. 13 mail/online deadline can still register and vote by going to their municipal clerk's office in person, including on Election Day itself — a more permissive rule than some other states (e.g., North Carolina, which restricts same-day registration to the early-voting window only).
RULES.detail: NEEDS REVIEW: sourced to Vote.gov's Maine registration guide; not independently cross-checked against the Maine SOS's own same-day-registration procedure page in this pass.

RULES.topic: Ranked-choice voting (RCV) scope — federal races only, general vs. primary
RULES.currentRule: Maine uses ranked-choice voting (RCV) for U.S. House, U.S. Senate, Governor, and State Legislature PRIMARIES, and for U.S. House, U.S. Senate, and President GENERAL elections (federal races only). RCV is NOT used for Governor or State Legislature GENERAL elections — a Maine Supreme Judicial Court advisory opinion in April 2026 blocked a proposed expansion of RCV to those general elections, maintaining the status quo.
RULES.whyItMatters: ME-02's general election (a U.S. House race) is formally subject to RCV rules. However, because only two candidates (Dunlap and LePage) qualified for the ballot, the race will effectively be decided by simple majority in the first count, since RCV multi-round tabulation only becomes operative with 3+ candidates and no first-round majority. If a third candidate qualifies before ballot certification, full RCV tabulation would apply as it did in the June 2026 Democratic primary.
RULES.detail: NEEDS REVIEW (watch item): reconfirm no late-qualifying write-in or third candidate emerges before ME-02's general-election ballot is finalized; if one does, full multi-round RCV tabulation would apply.

RULES.topic: Absentee ballot drop boxes — municipal discretion, no statewide locator
RULES.currentRule: Maine law (Title 21-A Section 752-B) permits, but does not require, municipal clerks to operate a secured drop box for absentee ballots. There is no statewide drop-box locator; availability, locations, and hours are set locally by each municipality. Drop boxes, where offered, are locked at 8:00 p.m. on Election Day.
RULES.whyItMatters: ME-02 voters cannot assume a drop box exists in their town. Voters should check their specific municipal clerk's website or contact the clerk's office directly to confirm whether a drop box is offered and where it is located.
RULES.detail: Confirmed via Title 21-A Section 752-B. Illustrative municipal examples (Freeport, Brunswick) are outside ME-02 and used only to show how local pages describe drop-box availability.

RULES.currentRule: Maine does not offer an online tool for voters to check their own registration status. The Maine SOS has explicitly confirmed this gap; voters must contact their municipal clerk directly to verify their registration.
RULES.whyItMatters: Unlike many other states, ME-02 voters cannot self-serve a registration-status check online. The dashboard's registration-status tile should direct users to their municipal clerk rather than implying an online lookup exists.
RULES.detail: Confirmed via Maine SOS's own 'General Election Day 2024 - 29 days away' release language ('Maine does not currently have an online registration lookup tool') and corroborated by Democracy Works; this is treated as a genuine tooling gap, not a research shortfall.

RULES.currentRule: If a returned absentee ballot's signature or affidavit is missing or does not match, the municipal clerk must attempt to contact the voter (within a day, or the day before/of the election) to allow curing. If unresolved, the voter may cast a different ballot in person by 8:00 p.m. on Election Day.
RULES.whyItMatters: ME-02 absentee voters whose ballot has a signature or affidavit issue have a path to cure it, but the clerk's contact window is narrow — voters should monitor their absentee ballot tracker and respond promptly if contacted.
RULES.detail: NEEDS REVIEW: sourced to the standing curing procedure described in a 2024-cycle Maine SOS release; not independently re-confirmed for the 2026 cycle in case of statutory change.

RULES.topic: Municipal (town/city) clerk administration model — no county election offices
RULES.currentRule: Maine elections are administered by town and city clerks, not counties. There is no county-level election office equivalent to Georgia's or North Carolina's county boards of elections. Each of ME-02's 10 whole counties and the 18 Kennebec County towns is served by its own municipal clerk's office. The Secretary of State's Bureau of Corporations, Elections & Commissions maintains a statewide directory of municipal clerks and registrars.
RULES.whyItMatters: ME-02 voters should contact their own town/city clerk, not a county office, for election administration questions. The dashboard's resource tiles route to statewide Maine SOS pages and the central BCEC contact rather than an exhaustive per-town office list.
RULES.detail: NEEDS REVIEW: exact direct URL to the 'Listing of Municipal Clerks and Registrars and Office Addresses' referenced on the Maine SOS Upcoming Elections page was not independently isolated in this pass. Fallback contact: Maine Elections Division, (207) 624-7650, cec.elections@maine.gov. A full itemized per-town clerk-office list for all of ME-02 was not compiled given the scale of Maine's decentralized administration model.

RULES.topic: ME-02 boundary definition — whole counties plus specific Kennebec towns
RULES.currentRule: Maine's congressional districts are defined by whole counties plus a list of specific towns, not a uniform county-based system. ME-02 covers 10 whole counties (Androscoggin, Aroostook, Franklin, Hancock, Oxford, Penobscot, Piscataquis, Somerset, Waldo, Washington) plus 18 specific Kennebec County towns (Augusta, Belgrade, Chelsea, Farmingdale, Fayette, Gardiner, Hallowell, Manchester, Monmouth, Mount Vernon, Oakland, Randolph, Readfield, Rome, Sidney, Vienna, Wayne, Winthrop). Maine's congressional boundaries have not been redrawn since the post-2020-census map.
RULES.whyItMatters: ME-02 voters in Kennebec County specifically must check whether their town is on the 18-town list — Kennebec County itself is split between ME-01 and ME-02, unlike the 10 whole counties.
RULES.detail: NEEDS REVIEW: the itemized 18-town Kennebec County list was corroborated only via Wikipedia in this pass; cross-check against the official Maine apportionment statute (Title 21-A) or Maine Legislature redistricting page before publishing as authoritative. The exact district map/plan document URL was also not independently re-fetched.
